contrary_evidence: Reducing exposure to like-minded sources on Facebook did not detectably reduce polarization in a 2023 experiment.
The 2018 exposure-to-opponents field experiment shows confrontational contact may increase disagreement.
2026 X algorithm findings distinguish changes in specific policy attitudes from nonsignificant polarization changes.
limitations: Datafolha 2026 reports perceived division, not a direct census of interpersonal hostility.
Cross-country associations between reported hostility, democracy and inequality are observational and survey instruments vary.
Classical philosophical works are conceptual frameworks, not comparable empirical estimates.
Platform experiments measure specific users and interventions over limited horizons, not guaranteed real-world effects.

en.title: The Dark Side of Politics: Why Struggles for Power Turn Disagreement into Hatred
en.deck: A historical, philosophical, psychological and political-economic investigation into collective identity, resentment, democratic rivalry and polarization in Brazil and across the world.
en.regime: Identity-based political conflict and declining intergroup trust
en.key_risk: Confusing policy disagreement with group-based dehumanization and attacks on democratic legitimacy
en.search_text: Political hostility, affective polarization, social identity theory, Brazil 2026, political economy, resentment and algorithmic amplification.
